note: Court rulings on laws that answer a catalog question the way a challenged law does, read September 29, 2026. Each row is one line of real rulings a judge reading a challenge to such a law would weigh: which way it cut (strike or uphold), how heavily (the shared decision scale: slight, moderate, strong, decisive), and what it held. A question with rulings both ways is left to each judge's own reading. None of these rulings decides a case in play by itself; see src/simulation/judiciary/judicial-review.ts. A ruling counts only from the day it was decided (decidedAt), so a world that opens before a ruling does not read it.
weightScale: HAND-SET: a U.S. Supreme Court holding directly on point is strong; a federal circuit or a state's highest court is moderate; a trial court, or a ruling on a neighboring question, is slight.

questions.question: us-policy-positions:technology-privacy.age-verification-for-social-media
questions.claim: the First Amendment right of adults and minors to read and speak online

rulings.cite: NetChoice v. Yost (S.D. Ohio Apr. 16, 2025); NetChoice v. Griffin (W.D. Ark. 2025)
rulings.held: requiring platforms to verify every user's age and get a parent's consent is not narrowly tailored

rulings.cite: Free Speech Coalition v. Paxton, 606 U.S. ___ (2025)
rulings.held: an age check on sexual material online is reviewed under intermediate scrutiny and stands, a neighboring question

rulings.cite: NetChoice v. Yost (6th Cir. June 18, 2026), stayed Aug. 17, 2026
rulings.held: the parental consent law can stand

questions.burdenOnState: A law that restricts speech by its content is reviewed under strict scrutiny, and the state must prove it narrowly tailored; the ordinary presumption that a statute is valid does not apply (NetChoice v. Yost, S.D. Ohio 2025, applying Reed v. Town of Gilbert, 576 U.S. 155 (2015)).

questions.question: us-policy-positions:environment-energy.ban-new-gas-hookups
questions.claim: preemption by the federal Energy Policy and Conservation Act

rulings.cite: California Restaurant Ass'n v. City of Berkeley, 89 F.4th 1094 (9th Cir. 2024)
rulings.held: a ban on gas piping in new buildings regulates the energy use of covered appliances, which federal law reserves

rulings.cite: Mulhern Gas Co. v. Mosley, No. 25-977 (2d Cir. June 30, 2026)
rulings.held: a ban on using gas appliances sets no energy conservation standard, so federal law does not preempt it

questions.question: us-policy-positions:education.public-funds-for-private-schooling
questions.claim: the state constitution's clauses on public money and the common schools

rulings.cite: Commonwealth ex rel. Cameron v. Johnson, 658 S.W.3d 25 (Ky. 2022); Adams v. McMaster (S.C. 2024)
rulings.held: public money for private schooling spends school funds outside the common schools

rulings.cite: Meredith v. Pence, 984 N.E.2d 1213 (Ind. 2013); Hart v. State, 774 S.E.2d 281 (N.C. 2015)
rulings.held: vouchers serve a public purpose and leave the public schools' own funding in place

rulings.cite: Crawford v. Marion County Election Board, 553 U.S. 181 (2008)
rulings.held: a photo identification requirement is justified by the state's interest in orderly elections
a state constitution's own voting clause can bar a photo requirement the federal Constitution allows

questions.question: us-policy-positions:justice-public-safety.end-cash-bail
questions.claim: the state constitution's bail and crime victims' clauses

rulings.held: the legislature may end monetary bail; the constitution does not require it

questions.question: us-policy-positions:justice-public-safety.permit-to-carry-concealed
questions.claim: the Second Amendment right to bear arms

rulings.cite: New York State Rifle & Pistol Ass'n v. Bruen, 597 U.S. 1, 38 n.9 (2022)
rulings.held: shall-issue permit requirements with objective criteria remain constitutional

questions.question: us-policy-positions:labor-workforce.right-to-work
questions.claim: the unions' property and free-association rights

rulings.cite: Sweeney v. Pence, 767 F.3d 654 (7th Cir. 2014); Zoeller v. Sweeney, 19 N.E.3d 749 (Ind. 2014)
rulings.held: barring mandatory union fees is not a taking of the union's property

rulings.cite: 74 Pinehurst LLC v. New York, 59 F.4th 557 (2d Cir. 2023), cert. denied (2024)
rulings.held: rent stabilization regulates the use of property and does not take it

questions.question: us-policy-positions:government-operations.independent-redistricting
questions.claim: the Elections Clause's grant to the legislature

rulings.cite: Arizona State Legislature v. Arizona Independent Redistricting Commission, 576 U.S. 787 (2015)
rulings.held: a state may give its line drawing to an independent commission
